title: pi-voice-telegram companion settings
description: Per-agent companion settings for the pi-voice-telegram extension. Edit and restart the agent session for changes to take effect. See README.md for the canonical key reference; this schema is the machine-readable form. The companion extension lives at `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-voice-telegram/` and reads this file at `~/.pi/agent/pi-voice-telegram.json` on each session start.

_hint.description: Free-form hint string. Ignored by the extension. Use as a place for an at-a-glance reminder of where the docs are; the extension never reads this field, but humans and LLMs inspecting the file will see it.

llm_tools.description: Controls the LLM-callable tool surface. The bridge's `telegram_attach` and `telegram_message` are always available; the companion's 7 LLM tools are gated on these flags. The `llm_tools.` namespace makes it explicit that these switches gate the LLM tool surface, not the TTS/STT extension features (which run unconditionally; only their LLM-tool wrappers are gated here).

exposed.description: Master switch for LLM tool registration. When false, none of the 7 LLM tools (synthesize_voice, transcribe_audio, pi_voice_telegram_schema, pi_voice_telegram_config_read / _write / _reset, pi_voice_telegram_list_voices) are registered. When true, registration is decided per-tool by `tools.<name>`. Operator preference (token-cost + ergonomic), not a security boundary. A sufficiently capable LLM with `bash` + `write` can modify this file regardless. Default false.

tools.description: Per-tool gates. Each LLM tool can be individually enabled/disabled. Each tool the LLM sees is added to its prompt, and per-tool gates let operators trim the surface (saves tokens + reduces the LLM's decision space, which helps for agents that get confused by too many tool choices). Defaults: all 7 `true` (back-compat with v0.16.10's `everything on when exposed: true` behavior). Honored only when `llm_tools.exposed` is true. v0.16.12: replaces the v0.16.10 `llm_tools.tts.enabled` and `llm_tools.stt.enabled` shortcuts — the old fields are silently ignored; configs that had them at `false` need to migrate to `tools.synthesize_voice: false` / `tools.transcribe_audio: false` to keep the previous behavior.

synthesize_voice.description: TTS tool: lets the LLM generate an OGG/Opus voice file on demand. When false, the LLM cannot call this tool mid-conversation; the bridge's mirror-mode auto-voice still works (it goes through the synthesis provider, not this tool). v0.16.12 default: true.

transcribe_audio.description: STT tool: lets the LLM transcribe a local audio file via whisper-server. When false, the LLM cannot call this tool; the v0.16.7 echo pipeline still transcribes every voice message automatically. v0.16.12 default: true.

pi_voice_telegram_schema.description: Returns the companion settings JSON Schema as text. Pure documentation primitive; no side effects, no cost. When false, the LLM has no way to discover the schema (would have to remember it). v0.16.12 default: true.

pi_voice_telegram_config_read.description: Reads the current `pi-voice-telegram.json` (full or per-key). Read-only, no cost, no side effects. When false, the LLM can't see its current config — `pi_voice_telegram_config_write` should also be `false` in that case (or the LLM would be writing blind). v0.16.12 default: true.

pi_voice_telegram_config_write.description: Writes a single key to `pi-voice-telegram.json`. Schema-validated (refuses unknown keys), atomic (write-to-tmp + rename), with `.bak.<unix-ms>` backups. The LLM can modify its own config. Set to `false` to freeze the config (LLM can read + list, but not modify). v0.16.12 default: true.

pi_voice_telegram_config_reset.description: Schema-driven reset to the current default config. Walks the JSON Schema, fills in any MISSING field with the schema's `default`, preserves the operator's existing values. Set to `false` to prevent the LLM from invoking the reset. v0.16.12 default: true.

pi_voice_telegram_list_voices.description: Returns the embedded 327-voice catalog (filterable by language / voiceName substring). Pure lookup primitive; lets the LLM find a valid voice ID instead of guessing and getting 2054 from MiniMax. v0.16.12 default: true.

tts.description: TTS tool name override. (The gate for the TTS tool was moved to `tools.synthesize_voice` in v0.16.12.)

name.description: Override the TTS tool name. Useful for namespace-collision avoidance. The description / promptSnippet / promptGuidelines text is templated against the resolved name (v0.8.0+), so renames are reflected in the LLM-facing strings.

stt.description: STT tool name override. (The gate for the STT tool was moved to `tools.transcribe_audio` in v0.16.12.)

name.description: Override the STT tool name. Same templating behavior as `llm_tools.tts.name`.

tts.description: Per-extension TTS defaults. Resolution order (highest priority first): explicit JSON value > matching env var (PI_MM_TTS_*) > hardcoded default. v0.8.0+. The synthesis provider reads these once per session_start and applies them to the bridge-driven TTS path AND the LLM-callable synthesize_voice tool. The bridge's `telegram.json` `outboundHandlers[voice].defaults.{voice,lang,rate}` keys still win for the bridge-owned bridge-driven path.

voice.description: Voice ID. Replaces $PI_MM_TTS_VOICE when present in JSON. MiniMax T2A API voice ID; the full list is shipped in this package as `voices.json` (327 voices across 24 languages) and surfaced to the agent via the `pi_voice_telegram_list_voices` tool — use that tool to discover valid IDs. A wrong ID returns 2054 with no in-band recovery. Prefer all-ASCII IDs (`Japanese_*`, `Cantonese_*` without full-width parens); see patches/v0.5.0/README.md for the §2a byte-trap details.

lang.description: Language boost passed to the TTS API. Replaces $PI_MM_TTS_LANG. Format is `Language,Dialect` (e.g. `Chinese,Yue` for Cantonese, `English,American` for en-US, `Chinese,Mandarin` for Mandarin, `Japanese` for Japanese). Independent of `voice` — `voice` is the speaker identity, `lang` is the pronunciation. Same-language voice+lang gives natural pronunciation; cross-language voice+lang is the 'boost' effect (e.g. Cantonese_PlayfulMan + lang=Japanese speaks with Japanese pronunciation via a Cantonese speaker).

model.description: TTS model ID. Replaces $PI_MM_TTS_MODEL. `speech-2.8-hd` is the high-def Cantonese-friendly default; older `speech-01`/`speech-02` legacy models have a 480-char per-chunk limit.

timeoutMs.description: Per-call synthesis timeout in ms. Covers both mm-tts HTTP and ffmpeg encoding. Replaces $PI_MM_TTS_VOICE_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS. Bump if you have long text inputs and see ffmpeg timeouts.

verifyAfterSynthesize.description: When true, run whisper-stt language detection on every synthesized OGG and record the result in the runtime event log under `category: "pi-voice-telegram/tts-verify"`. The event includes the requested `tts.lang`, the detected language (whisper's `detected_language`), confidence, and a `match` boolean. Catches the cross-language 'boost' misfires (e.g. voice=Cantonese_* + lang=Japanese producing audio that's neither) and gives the operator a per-call signal in the event log. Adds ~500ms–1s per synthesis (whisper-stt call). Off by default since v0.16.8 (was on in v0.16.0–v0.16.7); turn on for latency-tolerant paths where cross-language audio quality matters. v0.16.0+.

stt.description: Per-extension STT defaults. Resolution order (highest priority first): explicit JSON value > matching env var (PI_TELEGRAM_LANG, WHISPER_SERVER_URL, PI_TELEGRAM_STT_TIMEOUT_MS) > hardcoded default. v0.8.0+. The inbound echo AND the LLM-callable transcribe_audio tool both use these defaults.

lang.description: BCP-47 / ISO-639-1 language code. Replaces $PI_TELEGRAM_LANG. whisper-server uses this as the language hint for transcription.

baseUrl.description: whisper-server base URL. Replaces $WHISPER_SERVER_URL. The container shares network_mode: host with the host, so `127.0.0.1` is the host's whisper-server from inside the container.

timeoutMs.description: Per-call STT timeout in ms. Replaces $PI_TELEGRAM_STT_TIMEOUT_MS. Bump for long voice notes on slow GPUs.
